title: FACET: Multi-Agent AI Supporting Teachers in Scaling Differentiated Learning for Diverse Students
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of providing differentiated instruction in increasingly heterogeneous K–12 classrooms, where students vary in prior knowledge, motivation, language proficiency, and learning differences such as dyslexia and ADHD. The authors argue that while AI tools in education often promise personalization, most are student-facing and adapt primarily to performance, overlooking motivational and accessibility-related needs that shape learning. The paper asks whether a teacher-facing AI system can better support inclusive differentiation while preserving teacher autonomy and fitting into real school workflows.

To address this problem, the authors present FACET, a teacher-facing multi-agent AI framework for generating differentiated instructional materials. The system uses four coordinated agents: a learner agent that simulates different learner profiles, an assessment agent that diagnoses likely needs from those simulations, a generator agent that creates differentiated worksheets, and an evaluator agent that reviews output quality. FACET is designed as a teacher-in-the-loop system: teachers define learner profiles, upload or select materials, and review, edit, accept, or reject outputs. The framework incorporates curriculum guidance, scaffolding principles, and accessibility features intended to support learners with dyslexia and attention-related needs.

The empirical evaluation combines two components. First, two exploratory workshops were conducted with 30 German school principals to identify practical requirements for school deployment and classroom integration. Second, an online survey was conducted with 70 in-service K–12 teachers, primarily from the United Kingdom and United States, who reviewed five example grade-7 mathematics worksheets generated by FACET for different learner profiles. Teachers rated the materials on didactic structure, clarity, format/design, creativity, and, for the dyslexia-oriented worksheet, accessibility-related features such as readability and spacing.

The main conclusions are that FACET shows strong perceived value as a teacher support tool for differentiated instruction, especially for scaffolding-oriented materials and workflow support in heterogeneous classrooms. School leaders emphasized the need for curriculum alignment, accessibility, configurable learner profiles, and teacher control over outputs. Teachers generally rated worksheet structure and clarity positively, but enrichment-oriented materials for high-performing learners and dyslexia-specific formatting were rated less favorably, indicating areas for refinement. Overall, the study concludes that teacher-facing multi-agent AI can support inclusive differentiation at scale when designed around practitioner needs, though real classroom deployment and validation against authentic student responses remain future work.

identified_tools.name: FACET
identified_tools.description: A teacher-facing multi-agent AI framework for generating differentiated instructional materials using four coordinated agents for learner simulation, diagnostic assessment, material generation, and evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a teacher-in-the-loop system for generating grade 7 mathematics worksheets differentiated by learner profiles including performance, motivation, and dyslexia-related processing needs; evaluated via principal workshops and teacher quality ratings.

findings.finding_summary: In exploratory workshops, school principals reported strong perceived practical relevance for FACET as a differentiation support tool that could help address teacher workload, curriculum alignment, accessibility, and inclusive classroom needs. The study reports workshop participation from N = 30 principals, but no effect sizes or inferential statistics were reported.
findings.measure: Qualitative workshop themes on workflow integration, usability, and practical relevance

findings.finding_summary: Seventy K–12 teachers rated FACET-generated grade 7 mathematics worksheets favorably on didactic structure and clarity, especially for low-motivation profiles: Worksheet 1 had didactic structure M = 4.50 (SD = 1.02) and clarity M = 4.46 (SD = 1.05), while Worksheet 2 had didactic structure M = 4.41 (SD = 1.06) and clarity M = 4.23 (SD = 1.16) on a 6-point scale. However, the enrichment worksheet for high-performing, highly motivated learners received lower ratings across dimensions (structure M = 3.87, clarity M = 3.57, format M = 3.10, creativity M = 3.30), suggesting stronger performance for scaffolded than enrichment-oriented materials.
findings.measure: Teacher ratings of worksheet quality for mathematics materials on didactic structure, clarity, format/design, and creativity (6-point Likert scale)

findings.finding_summary: For the dyslexia-adapted mathematics worksheet, teachers rated spacing/layout M = 4.07 (SD = 1.39) and language simplification M = 3.94 (SD = 1.40), indicating partial alignment with accessibility goals. But font readability was rated M = 3.30 (SD = 1.61) and suitability for reading difficulties M = 3.46 (SD = 1.47), showing room for improvement in typographical adaptation for dyslexia-related needs.
findings.measure: Teacher ratings of dyslexia-adapted worksheet accessibility: suitability for reading difficulties, font readability, language simplification, spacing and layout

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods study using qualitative workshops and descriptive survey ratings rather than an RCT or quasi-experimental design. It provides empirical usability and perceived-quality evidence, but no causal estimates of student learning effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports generally favorable perceptions of material quality and practical value, but impact on actual student outcomes is unclear and no standardized effect sizes are reported. Findings are promising but limited to perceived quality and implementation potential.
